doc.name: A — luggage catalogue, backlit silhouette, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: polycarbonate carry-on
Category: luggage
Shot programme: backlit silhouette
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a luggage catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the group with variants in a backlit silhouette treatment.

SUBJECT. A polycarbonate carry-on. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Product with two colourway or size siblings in stepped depth. Shoot on a 70-200mm zoom at 150mm at f/22, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a hard fresnel through an egg-crate grid for a crisp-edged shadow. Stage the product on or against brushed aluminium, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a bleach-bypass look with crushed saturation and lifted contrast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

config.system_prompt:
You are a commercial stills director briefing a luggage capture. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the top-down flat in a backlit silhouette treatment.

SUBJECT. A polycarbonate carry-on. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Directly overhead, product and props arranged on a single plane. Shoot on a 50mm normal at f/11, framing for rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-left with open air to the right.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with an overcast soft dome with no directional shadow at all. Stage the product on or against cast pigmented resin, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a sun-bleached grade with faded blacks and a green-yellow bias. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.
